vsm1.7:107.1: One who wants to develop the recollection of generosity
vsm1.7:107.2: should be naturally devoted to generosity and the constant practice of giving and sharing.
vsm1.7:107.3: Or alternatively, if he is one who is starting the development of it,
vsm1.7:107.4:
he should make the resolution: “From now on, when there is anyone present to receive,
I shall not eat even a single mouthful without having given a gift.”
vsm1.7:107.5:
And that very day he should give a gift by sharing according to his means
and his ability with those who have distinguished qualities.
vsm1.7:107.6: When he has apprehended the sign in that,
vsm1.7:107.7:
he should go into solitary retreat and recollect his own generosity in its special
qualities of being free from the stain of avarice, etc., as follows:
vsm1.7:107.8: “It is gain for me, it is great gain for me,
vsm1.7:107.9: that in a generation obsessed by the stain of avarice I abide with my heart free from stain by avarice,
vsm1.7:107.10:
and am freely generous and open-handed, that I delight in relinquishing,
expect to be asked, and rejoice in giving and sharing” (A III 287).
vsm1.7:108.1: Herein, it is gain for me: it is my gain, advantage.
vsm1.7:108.2:
The intention is: I surely partake of those kinds of gain for a giver that have been commended by the Blessed One as follows:
“A man who gives life by giving food shall have life either divine or human” (A III 42),
vsm1.7:108.3: and: “A giver is loved and frequented by many” (A III 40),
vsm1.7:108.4: and: “One who gives is ever loved, according to the wise man’s law” (A III 41), and so on.
vsm1.7:109.1: It is great gain for me: it is great gain for me that this Dispensation, or the human state, has been gained by me.
vsm1.7:109.3: Because of the fact that “I abide with my mind free from stain by avarice … and rejoice in giving and sharing.”
vsm1.7:110.1: Herein, obsessed by the stain of avarice is overwhelmed by the stain of avarice.
vsm1.7:110.2: Generation: beings, so called owing to the fact of their being generated.
vsm1.7:110.3:
So the meaning here is this: among beings who are overwhelmed by the stain of avarice,
which is one of the dark states that corrupt the natural transparency of consciousness (see A I
10) and which has the characteristic of inability to bear sharing one’s own good fortune with others.
vsm1.7:111.1: Free from stain by avarice because of being both free from avarice and from the other stains, greed, hate, and the rest.
vsm1.7:111.2: I abide with my heart: I abide with my consciousness of the kind already stated, is the meaning.
vsm1.7:111.3:
But in the sutta, “I live the home life with my heart free” (A III 287; V 331), etc., is said because it was taught there
as a mental abiding to depend on constantly to Mahānāma the Sakyan, who was a stream-enterer asking about an abiding to depend on.
vsm1.7:111.4: There the meaning is “I live overcoming …”
vsm1.7:112.2: Open-handed: with hands that are purified.
vsm1.7:112.3: What is meant is: with hands that are always washed in order to give gifts carefully with one’s own hands.
vsm1.7:112.4: That I delight in relinquishing: the act of relinquishing (vossajjana) is relinquishing (vossagga); the meaning is, giving up.
vsm1.7:112.5: To delight in relinquishing is to delight in constant devotion to that relinquishing.
vsm1.7:112.6: Expect to be asked (yācayoga): accustomed to being asked (yācana-yogga) because of giving whatever others ask for, is the meaning.
vsm1.7:112.7: Yājayoga is a reading, in which case the meaning is: devoted (yutta) to sacrifice (yāja), in other words, to sacrificing (yajana).
vsm1.7:112.9: the meaning is, he recollects thus: “I give gifts and I share out what is to be used by myself, and I rejoice in both.”
vsm1.7:113.1: As long as he recollects his own generosity in its special qualities of freedom from stain by avarice, etc., in this way,
vsm1.7:113.2: then: “On that occasion his mind is not obsessed by greed,
vsm1.7:113.3: or obsessed by hate, or obsessed by delusion;
vsm1.7:113.4: his mind has rectitude on that occasion, being inspired by generosity” (A III 287).
vsm1.7:113.5: So when he has suppressed the hindrances in the way already described (§66),
vsm1.7:113.6: the jhāna factors arise in a single conscious moment.
vsm1.7:113.7:
But owing to the profundity of the generosity’s special qualities, or owing to his being occupied in recollecting
the generosity’s special qualities of many sorts,
vsm1.7:113.8: the jhāna is only access and does not reach absorption.
vsm1.7:113.9:
And that access jhāna is known as “recollection of generosity” too because it
arises with the generosity’s special qualities as the means.
vsm1.7:114.1: And when a bhikkhu is devoted to this recollection of generosity, he becomes ever more intent on generosity,
vsm1.7:114.3: he acts in conformity with loving-kindness,
vsm1.7:114.5: He has much happiness and gladness.
vsm1.7:114.6: And if he penetrates no higher, he is at least headed for a happy destiny.
vsm1.7:114.7:
Now, when a man is truly wise,
His constant task will surely be
This recollection of his giving
Blessed with such mighty potency.
vsm1.7:114.8: This is the section dealing with the recollection of generosity in the detailed explanation.
vsm1.7:115.1: One who wants to develop the recollection of deities
vsm1.7:115.2: should possess the special qualities of faith, etc., evoked by means of the noble path,
vsm1.7:115.3:
and he should go into solitary retreat and recollect his own special qualities of faith,
etc., with deities standing as witnesses, as follows:
vsm1.7:115.4:
“There are deities of the Realm of the Four Kings (devā cātummahārājikā), there are deities of the Realm of the Thirty-three
(devā tāvatiṃsā), there are deities who are Gone to Divine Bliss (yāmā) … who are Contented (tusitā) … who
Delight in Creating (nimmānarati) … who Wield Power Over Others’ Creations (paranimmitavasavatti),
vsm1.7:115.5: there are deities of Brahmā’s Retinue (brahmakāyikā), there are deities higher than that.
vsm1.7:115.6: And those deities were possessed of faith such that on dying here they were reborn there, and such faith is present in me too.
vsm1.7:115.7: And those deities were possessed of virtue … of learning … of generosity …
vsm1.7:115.8: of understanding such that when they died here they were reborn there, and such understanding is present in me too” (A III 287).
vsm1.7:116.1:
In the sutta, however, it is said: “On the occasion, Mahānāma, on which a noble disciple recollects the faith,
the virtue, the learning, the generosity, and the understanding that are both his own and of those deities,”
vsm1.7:116.2: on that occasion his mind is not obsessed by greed …” (A III 287).
vsm1.7:116.4:
it should nevertheless be understood as said for the purpose of showing that the special qualities of faith,
etc., in oneself are those in the deities, making the deities stand as witnesses.
vsm1.7:116.5: For it is said definitely in the Commentary: “He recollects his own special qualities, making the deities stand as witnesses.”
vsm1.7:117.1: As long as in the prior stage he recollects the deities’ special qualities of faith, etc.,
vsm1.7:117.2: and in the later stage he recollects the special qualities of faith, etc., existing in himself,
vsm1.7:117.3: then: “On that occasion his mind is not obsessed by greed,
vsm1.7:117.4: or obsessed by hate, or obsessed by delusion,
vsm1.7:117.5: his mind has rectitude on that occasion, being inspired by deities” (A III 288).
vsm1.7:117.6: So when he has suppressed the hindrances in the way already stated (§66), the jhāna factors arise in a single conscious moment.
vsm1.7:117.7:
But owing to the profundity of the special qualities of faith,
etc., or owing to his being occupied in recollecting special qualities of many sorts,
vsm1.7:117.8: the jhāna is only access and does not reach absorption.
vsm1.7:117.9:
And that access jhāna itself is known as “recollection of deities” too because it
arises with the deities special qualities as the means.
vsm1.7:118.1: And when a bhikkhu is devoted to this recollection of deities, he becomes dearly loved by deities.
vsm1.7:118.2: He obtains even greater fullness of faith.
vsm1.7:118.3: He has much happiness and gladness.
vsm1.7:118.4: And if he penetrates no higher, he is at least headed for a happy destiny.
vsm1.7:118.5:
Now, when a man is truly wise,
His constant task will surely be
This recollection of deities
Blessed with such mighty potency.
vsm1.7:118.6: This is the section dealing with the recollection of deities in the detailed explanation.
vsm1.7:119.1:
Now, in setting forth the detail of these recollections, after the words, “His mind
has rectitude on that occasion, being inspired by the Perfect One,”
vsm1.7:119.2: it is added: “When a noble disciple’s mind has rectitude, Mahānāma, the meaning inspires him, the law inspires him,
vsm1.7:119.3: and the application of the law makes him glad. When he is glad, happiness is born in him” (A III 285–88).
vsm1.7:119.4:
Herein, the meaning inspires him should be understood as said of contentment inspired by the meaning
beginning, “This Blessed One is such since he is …” (§2).
vsm1.7:119.5: The law inspires him is said of contentment inspired by the text.
vsm1.7:119.6: The application of the law makes him glad is said of both (cf. M-a I 173).
vsm1.7:120.1: And when in the case of the recollection of deities inspired by deities is said,
vsm1.7:120.2: this should be understood as said either of the consciousness that occurs in the prior stage inspired by deities
vsm1.7:120.3:
or of the consciousness that occurs in the later stage inspired by the special qualities
that are similar to those of the deities and are productive of the deities’ state (cf. §117).
vsm1.7:121.1: These six recollections succeed only in noble disciples.
vsm1.7:121.2: For the special qualities of the Enlightened One, the Law, and the Community, are evident to them;
vsm1.7:121.3: and they possess the virtue with the special qualities of untornness, etc.,
vsm1.7:121.4: the generosity that is free from stain by avarice,
vsm1.7:121.5: and the special qualities of faith, etc., similar to those of deities.
vsm1.7:122.1:
And in the Mahānāma Sutta (A III 285 f.) they are expounded in detail by the Blessed One in order to show
a stream-winner an abiding to depend upon when he asked for one.
vsm1.7:123.1:
Also in the Gedha Sutta they are expounded in order that a noble disciple should purify
his consciousness by means of the recollections and so attain further purification in the ultimate sense thus:
vsm1.7:123.2: “Here, bhikkhus, a noble disciple recollects the Perfect One in this way: That Blessed One is such since he is accomplished …
vsm1.7:123.3: His mind has rectitude on that occasion. He has renounced, got free from, emerged from cupidity.
vsm1.7:123.4: Cupidity, bhikkhus, is a term for the five cords of sense desire.
vsm1.7:123.5: Some beings gain purity here by making this recollection their prop” (A III 312).
vsm1.7:124.1:
And in the Sambādhokāsa Sutta taught by the venerable Mahā-Kaccāna they are expounded as the realization of the wide-open
through the susceptibility of purification that exists in the ultimate sense only in a noble disciple thus:
vsm1.7:124.2: “It is wonderful, friends, it is marvellous
vsm1.7:124.4: that is to say, the six stations of recollection. What six?
vsm1.7:124.5:
Here, friends, a noble disciple recollects the Perfect One … Some beings
are susceptible to purification in this way” (A III 314–15).
vsm1.7:125.1:
Also in the Uposatha Sutta they are expounded in order to show the greatness of the fruit of the Uposatha,
as a mind-purifying meditation subject for a noble disciple who is observing the Uposatha:
vsm1.7:125.2: “And what is the Noble Ones’ Uposatha, Visākhā?
vsm1.7:125.3: It is the gradual cleansing of the mind still sullied by imperfections.
vsm1.7:125.4: And what is the gradual cleansing of the mind still sullied by imperfections?
vsm1.7:125.5: Here, Visākhā, a noble disciple recollects the Perfect One …” (A I 206–11).
vsm1.7:126.1:
And in the Book of Elevens, when a noble disciple has asked, “Venerable sir, in what way should we abide who
abide in various ways?” (A V 328), they are expounded to him in order to show the way of abiding in this way:
vsm1.7:126.2: “One who has faith is successful, Mahānāma, not one who has no faith.
vsm1.7:126.3:
One who is energetic … One whose mindfulness is established … One who is concentrated … One who
has understanding is successful, Mahānāma, not one who has no understanding.
vsm1.7:126.4: Having established yourself in these five things, Mahānāma, you should develop six things.
vsm1.7:126.5: Here, Mahānāma, you should recollect the Perfect One: That Blessed One is such since …” (A V 329–32).
vsm1.7:127.1:
Still, though this is so, they can be brought to mind by an ordinary man too,
if he possesses the special qualities of purified virtue, and the rest.
vsm1.7:127.2:
For when he is recollecting the special qualities of the Buddha, etc.,
even only according to hearsay, his consciousness settles down,
vsm1.7:127.3: by virtue of which the hindrances are suppressed.
vsm1.7:127.4: In his supreme gladness he initiates insight,
vsm1.7:127.5: and he even attains to Arahantship, like the Elder Phussadeva who dwelt at Kaṭakandhakāra.
vsm1.7:128.1: That venerable one, it seems, saw a figure of the Enlightened One created by Māra.
vsm1.7:128.2: He thought, “How good this appears despite its having greed, hate and delusion!
vsm1.7:128.3: What can the Blessed One’s goodness have been like?
vsm1.7:128.4: For he was quite without greed, hate and delusion!”
vsm1.7:128.5: He acquired happiness with the Blessed One as object, and by augmenting his insight he reached Arahantship.
vsm1.7:128.6:
The seventh chapter called “The Description of Six
Recollections” in the Treatise on the Development of
Concentration in the Path of Purification composed for the
purpose of gladdening good people.
